top_findings.author: @coreyganim
top_findings.summary: Corey Ganim posted a thread explaining 'The 80/20 of Hermes Agent for non-technical people' — describing it as an open-source AI agent that runs 24/7 on a $5 server and messages through Telegram, Discord, or WhatsApp. He compares Hermes with OpenClaw, noting Hermes adds a learning loop where every ~15 actions it reflects and improves. This is significant visibility for Hermes Agent.

top_findings.author: @tom_doerr
top_findings.summary: New open-source local AI desktop agent called 'Accomplish' launched. GitHub: github.com/accomplish-ai/accomplish. Represents a new entrant in the local AI agent space, competing with OpenClaw and similar frameworks.

top_findings.author: @RoundtableSpace
top_findings.summary: Someone open sourced a full Claude Code stack with 27 agents, 64 skills, and 33 commands. Includes planning, reviews, fixes, token optimization, and built-in security checks. This is a major acceleration of the Claude Code ecosystem and raises the bar for agent framework completeness.

top_findings.author: @hasantoxr
top_findings.summary: AI-Trader is an open source marketplace where AI agents publish trading signals, debate strategies with each other, and execute trades across 7 asset classes fully autonomously. OpenClaw agents can join with one command. Very high engagement (1.1K likes) suggests strong community interest in autonomous multi-agent marketplaces.

top_findings.category: New product from major AI lab
top_findings.author: @futureradar_FR
top_findings.summary: Anthropic announced 'Claude Managed Agents' — positioning it as a major developer productivity play that eliminates complex infrastructure and months of setup. Described as making 'months of work obsolete for developers.' This is Anthropic's formal entry into the managed agent space, competing with self-hosted solutions like Hermes and OpenClaw.
